source.title: The Geometry of Categorical and Hierarchical Concepts in Large Language Models
source.authors: Kiho Park; Yo Joong Choe; Yi-Bo Jiang; Victor Veitch

record.tranche_reason: The paper measures linear feature and category geometry in LLMs, but does not test superposition, polysemanticity, SAE recovery, or whether superposed features are one-dimensional. Its discussion mentions toy-model polytopes and SAE interpretability, without testing those claims.
record.gate_note: The reported measurements concern WordNet feature representations, hierarchical orthogonality, and categorical polytopes. They do not measure feature overlap caused by capacity pressure, sparsity or importance, neuron polysemanticity, or SAE feature completeness. Adjacent geometric findings are recorded under fits_no_version; none of the claim versions is tested.
record.test_reason: The paper estimates linear vector representations of WordNet concepts in the final-layer unembedding space of Gemma-2B and LLaMA-3-8B. It tests hierarchical orthogonality and polytope structure. It does not measure superposition, sparsity or capacity effects, neuron polysemanticity, or SAE feature recovery or quality. Superposition-related material appears only in the Discussion: polytopes observed in toy models (Elhage et al.), and an argument that SAE features for hierarchical concepts would be co-linear. Neither is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors extend the linear representation hypothesis from directions to vectors and polytopes, prove that hierarchy implies orthogonality, and validate this on Gemma-2B and LLaMA-3-8B using 900+ WordNet concepts. They also argue that SAEs seeking separate binary features for hierarchical concepts would face co-linear directions, and they note that the method applies only to the final layer.
record.recipe_differences: The paper estimates WordNet feature vectors from whitened unembedding vectors using an LDA variant, and evaluates hierarchical and categorical geometry in LLMs; it does not use the original toy-network superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported hierarchical orthogonality depends on the causal inner product: the authors report it is not satisfied using the naive Euclidean inner product. Shuffled unembeddings and whether token-set inclusion is broken also affect the control result.

fits_no_version.finding: In Gemma-2B, LDA-estimated WordNet noun feature vectors give test-word projections near 1 and random-word projections near 0. Shuffled unembeddings remove this structure.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Most WordNet noun attributes have approximately linear vector representations in Gemma-2B's final-layer, causally whitened unembedding space.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding a parent-contrast vector shifts parent logit differences by 5.1 to 14.4. Child logit differences shift by -0.15 to 0.38, with SDs of about 1.1 to 1.5.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the reported Gemma-2B examples, estimated parent-contrast vectors alter the target concept selectively, leaving subordinate concepts largely unchanged.

fits_no_version.finding: Parent vectors are near-orthogonal to child-minus-parent vectors under the causal inner product in Gemma-2B and LLaMA-3-8B. A random-parent control is far from orthogonal. The result survives breaking set inclusion, but fails under the Euclidean inner product.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: WordNet hierarchy is encoded as orthogonality of concept vectors under the causal inner product, and the effect depends on the choice of inner product.

fits_no_version.finding: Most WordNet noun features have estimated vector representations in LLaMA-3-8B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Most tested WordNet noun attributes have approximately linear vector representations in LLaMA-3-8B's unembedding space.

record.problems: The empirical study concerns final-layer unembedding geometry and depends on a causal-inner-product whitening transformation; the authors state that the method only works for the final layer. Most figure values are reported qualitatively in the text rather than numerically. The geometric results do not measure superposition or neuron-level feature allocation.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted additional analogous WordNet verb-hierarchy results (Figures 13–16) and further Gemma/LLaMA-3 hierarchy plots (Figures 4, 10, 14, 18, and 20); these repeat the same geometric measurements and are not direct tests of the claim versions.

untested.parts: No toy networks, feature count above dimension, sparsity sweeps, or superposition geometry. The paper only cites toy-model polytopes as something its theory may explain.
No neuron-level analysis, capacity competition, or importance-dependent allocation.
No analysis of the causes of polysemantic neurons.
No measurement of feature spread across neurons and no dictionary or SAE recovery. The WordNet vectors are supervised LDA directions in the unembedding space.
No SAE is trained or evaluated. The claim that SAE features for animal, mammal and bird would be 'strongly co-linear, and potentially difficult to disentangle' is a Discussion argument, not a result.
Binary features are estimated as vectors and categorical concepts as polytopes or subspaces. No test compares 1-D and multi-dimensional superposed features.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T6/discusses classification stands. The superposition-adjacent content is limited to two Discussion remarks: toy-model polytopes and SAE co-linearity. Neither is an empirical test, so no verdict labels are given. The row states are consistent with the text. Also not recorded as rows, and bearing on no version: the random-parent control in Figure 5 and the polytope visualisations (Figures 2 and 6), which use tokens generated by ChatGPT-4.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks, feature-over-capacity conditions, sparsity-dependent transitions, or superposition geometry are tested.
No neuron polysemanticity, capacity competition, or importance-dependent allocation of dimensions is tested.
No alternative causes of polysemantic neurons are tested.
The paper does not measure feature spread across neurons or recovery of sparse features by a dictionary/SAE.
No SAE feature completeness, stability, or canonicity is evaluated.

The paper estimates vector representations for binary concepts and polytopes for categorical concepts, but does not test whether features involved in superposition are one-dimensional or multidimensional.

rows.subject: Gemma-2B
rows.operation_detail: Fit LDA vector representations to WordNet noun features and measure projections of vocabulary unembeddings
rows.measure: Projection of train, test, and random words on estimated feature vectors, normalized by vector magnitude
rows.value: Test projections are near 1 and random-word projections are near 0; train, test, and random means and standard deviations are plotted, with exact values not stated
rows.uncertainty: Standard deviations shown in figure; exact values not stated
rows.note: The paper describes these results as evidence that vector representations exist for the features; this is not a measurement of superposition.
